## Script Summary 
- Downloads raw mutation data using TCGAbiolinks queries
- 33 total cancer types
- Creates SummarizedExperiment objects for each cancer type 

## Set up
```{r projects to download}
projects <- c(
  "TCGA-BRCA", "TCGA-OV","TCGA-GBM", "TCGA-LUAD", "TCGA-UCEC", 
  "TCGA-KIRC", "TCGA-HNSC", "TCGA-LGG", "TCGA-THCA", "TCGA-LUSC", 
  "TCGA-PRAD", "TCGA-SKCM", "TCGA-COAD", "TCGA-STAD", "TCGA-BLCA", 
  "TCGA-LIHC", "TCGA-CESC", "TCGA-KIRP", "TCGA-SARC", "TCGA-LAML", 
  "TCGA-ESCA", "TCGA-PAAD", "TCGA-PCPG", "TCGA-READ", "TCGA-TGCT", 
  "TCGA-THYM", "TCGA-KICH", "TCGA-ACC", "TCGA-MESO", "TCGA-UVM", 
  "TCGA-DLBC", "TCGA-UCS", "TCGA-CHOL"
)

#Sets the CBMDATA directory path
Sys.setenv(CBMDATA = "/restricted/projectnb/agedisease/CBMrepositoryData")

#Combines CBMDATA path with sub-directories for data output
PATH <- file.path(Sys.getenv("CBMDATA"), "TCGA-GDC", "mutation", "raw_data")
PATH_rawdl <- file.path(PATH,"project_downloads")
PATH_se <- file.path(PATH,"raw_SE")
```


## Downloading Raw Data - Function
Here we use TCGAbiolinks to download the mutation data from all TCGA projects. 
- This script (in its current form) only includes primary tumor data
- It creates a SummarizedExperiment object with GDCprepare()

More info on queries:
https://bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/vignettes/TCGAbiolinks/inst/doc/query.html

More information on DNAseq analysis pipeline for TCGA: https://docs.gdc.cancer.gov/Data/Bioinformatics_Pipelines/DNA_Seq_Variant_Calling_Pipeline/
More information on Mutation Annotation Format (Masked Somatic Mutation files): https://docs.gdc.cancer.gov/Data/File_Formats/MAF_Format/

MAF Reading and Binary Matrix Creation: Mutation Annotation Format (MAF) files are processed with maftools::read.maf to convert mutation counts into a binary format indicating the presence or absence of mutations in each sample for each gene.

Mutation Type-Specific Processing
- Binary Matrix Generation: For each type of mutation, a separate binary matrix is generated. This matrix undergoes processing to ensure it reflects primary tumor samples only, and sample identifiers are appropriately shortened and deduplicated.

- Mapping to Full Matrix: Each mutation type's data is then mapped to a full matrix representing all possible genes and samples, facilitating easier comparative analyses across different mutation types.

These different categories of mutations (along with the full binary matrix) are packaged into a SummarizedExperiment object as assays. 

```{r Download project data}
## download of the TCGA project dataset for RPPA
data_download <- function(project) {
  project.hg38 <- TCGAbiolinks::GDCquery(
    project = project,
    data.category = "Simple Nucleotide Variation", 
    data.type = "Masked Somatic Mutation",
    access = "open"
  )

  # Download query
  GDCdownload(project.hg38, directory = PATH_rawdl)
  # Assign query to global variable
  assign(paste0(project, "_query.hg38"), project.hg38, envir = .GlobalEnv)
}


## This will create and download data to "GDCdata" folder in PATH_rawdl directory
for (project in projects) {
  cat("Downloading mutation data for", project, "\n") # Print message to keep track
  
  #download data with query
  data_download(project)
  
  #retrieve query variable
  data_name<- paste0(project, "_query.hg38")
  query_obj <- get(data_name)
  data.hg38 <- GDCprepare(query_obj, directory = PATH_rawdl, summarizedExperiment = TRUE)
  
  
  ### BINARY FORMAT ###
  #read maf
  maf <- maftools::read.maf(data.hg38)
  mutation_data <- as.data.frame(maf@data)
  binary_matrix <- table(mutation_data$Tumor_Sample_Barcode, mutation_data$Hugo_Symbol)
  binary_matrix[binary_matrix > 0] <- 1
  
  # Convert the matrix to a data frame for easier viewing and manipulation
  mut_genes<-t(binary_matrix)

  # Convert the matrix to a data frame for easier viewing and manipulation
  mut_genes <- mut_genes[, grepl("-01", colnames(mut_genes))]
  colnames(mut_genes) = substr(colnames(mut_genes), 1, 12)
  

  unique_cols <- !duplicated(colnames(mut_genes))
  mut_genes <- mut_genes[, unique_cols]
  
  # Unique genes and samples from the MAF object
  all_genes <- rownames(mut_genes)
  all_samples <- colnames(mut_genes)

  # Store all matrices
  list_matrices <- list(all = mut_genes )

  #PER MUTATION TYPE
# Loop over each type of mutation to create binary matrices
  for (type in unique(mutation_data$Variant_Classification)) {
      # Generate the mutation count matrix for the current mutation type
      mut_mat <- maftools::mutCountMatrix(maf, includeSyn = FALSE, countOnly = type, removeNonMutated = FALSE)
      
      # Convert counts to binary (if there are multiple mutations of the same type, they need to be consolidated)
      mut_mat <- ifelse(mut_mat > 0, 1, 0)
      
      # Filter to primary tumors only and shorten barcodes
      mut_mat <- mut_mat[, grepl("-01", colnames(mut_mat))]
      colnames(mut_mat) = substr(colnames(mut_mat), 1, 12)
      
      #remove duplicate samples
      unique_cols <- !duplicated(colnames(mut_mat))
      mut_mat <- mut_mat[, unique_cols]
      
      # Create an empty matrix with the correct dimensions
      full_matrix <- matrix(0, nrow = length(all_genes), ncol = length(all_samples),
                            dimnames = list(all_genes, all_samples))
      
      # Match rows and columns from mut_mat to full_matrix
      row_inds <- match(rownames(mut_mat), rownames(full_matrix))
      col_inds <- match(colnames(mut_mat), colnames(full_matrix))
      
      # Loop through each non-zero element in mut_mat and map it to full_matrix
      for (i in seq_along(row_inds)) {
          if (!is.na(row_inds[i])) {
              for (j in seq_along(col_inds)) {
                  if (!is.na(col_inds[j]) && mut_mat[i, j] == 1) {
                      full_matrix[row_inds[i], col_inds[j]] <- 1
                  }
              }
          }
      }
      # Verify the mapping accuracy
      if (sum(mut_mat) != sum(full_matrix)) {
          cat("Mismatch in sum for type", type, ": mut_mat =", sum(mut_mat), ", final =", sum(full_matrix), "\n")
      } else {
          list_matrices[[type]] <- full_matrix 
      }
  }


  # Create the SummarizedExperiment object
  binary_se <- SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment(assays = list_matrices)
  
  # Save data
  SE_output_filename <- paste0(project, "_binary-mutation.rds")
  saveRDS(binary_se, file = file.path(PATH_se, SE_output_filename))
  
  # Optional: Adds a delay of 5 seconds between downloads to avoid overwhelming the server
  Sys.sleep(5)
}

```
